title: Tenant streaming connection stalls: synthetic timeout shim and adaptive fast-fail escalation playbook
creator: Daniel Kim
description:
Summary:
We observed multiple customer escalations driven by long-running streaming requests that converted into 5xx waves and tenant-level retries. Root cause appears to be intermittent stalls inside the edge-to-backend streaming path: long-tail kernel scheduling combined with occasional KV-cache compaction pauses and proxy keepalive interactions. These stalls leave connections open without progress, causing client SDKs to retry aggressively which amplifies load and trips downstream capacity protections.

What this ticket does:
1) Ship a short-lived synthetic-timeout shim at the edge that injects an upper bound for idle-in-stream progress (configurable per-route and per-tenant). The shim triggers a controlled fast-fail (RFC style) to let the client choose backoff rather than relying on network timeouts.
2) Implement an adaptive fast-fail policy: per-tenant inflight caps + a degradation token that ages out with observed recovery.
3) Add targeted observability: streaming_stall_count, last_progress_ms, tenant_headroom, and request_fingerprint to identify pre-failure patterns.
4) Provide an escalation playbook and runbook for support to triage and temporarily opt affected tenants into a conservative fast-fail profile.

Reproduction steps (dev env):
- Use streaming client (sdk-psi) against canary edge with artificially delayed backend (sleep 2-10s per chunk)
- Enable KV-compaction hook in dev runtime to emulate STA pauses
- Run parallel 200 tenant-simulated connections with exponential retry backoff disabled
- Observe stalled streams not emitting progress and client retries amplifying the load

Investigation notes / hypothesis:
- Kernel/task scheduler hotspots: large batches + long KV eviction cycles cause worker threads to enter short (200ms-2s) unresponsive windows. During these windows, streaming keepalives are not processed leading clients to assume silent failure.
- Edge proxy keepalive defaults (60s) are too large for our streaming semantics; many SDKs implement aggressive client retry heuristics at lower thresholds.
- Lack of a graceful fast-fail path forces Kafka-like retry storms through the system rather than letting clients back off.

Mitigation (short-term):
- Deploy synthetic-timeout shim to edge: default idle_progress_timeout_ms=1500, per-route override allowed. The shim closes streams with a deterministic 526 body containing structured retry guidance.
- Add per-tenant inflight cap at proxy (default 40 concurrent streams). Excess attempts receive immediate 429 with Retry-After.
- Emergency canary rollout: 10% of traffic in us-east-1 -> monitor for collateral error/latency regressions.

Longer-term work (follow-ups after stabilization):
- Improve runtime scheduler preemption and reduce KV compaction pause variance (ENG-runtime team epics).
- Integrate SDK semantics with platform: add explicit client backoff header support and idempotency tokens for streaming resumability.
- Add automated tenant-level throttling controller that negotiates headroom with the autoscaler to prevent amplification.

Rollout plan:
1) Code ready and unit tested (this ticket) -> small canary in us-east-1 (10% tenants) for 24h with dashboards watching streaming_stall_count, 5xx_rate, retry-amplification-index.
2) If canary shows >0.5% collateral latency regressions, rollback immediate and instrument additional tracing.
3) Gradual 25/50/100% expansion over 72h with human-in-the-loop approvals.

Communication & support:
- Provide support-runbook: instructions to opt a tenant into conservative-profile (idle_progress_timeout_ms=5000, inflight_cap=10) and a one-click opt-out.
- Slack escalation channel: #inc-hosted-api-escalations -> notify on canary thresholds.
- Customer comms draft for high-impact customers included in attachments.

Backports / applicability to Dedicated / Private:
- Synthetic-timeout shim implemented in edge proxy but included as a configurable policy that can be enabled on Dedicated and Private control planes. For Private, provide a Kubernetes-sidecar option and kyverno policy examples.

Acceptance criteria:
- Synthetic timeout shim deployed to canary and verified by injected fault tests reducing retry-amplification-index by >=60% for simulated stalls.
- New streaming metrics visible on Console per-route and per-tenant.
- Support runbook validated by on-call (one dry-run opt-in/out).

Links: see attachments and linked PRs for implementation details.

2025-02-16: Canary rollout started in us-east-1 10% traffic. After 6 hours observed 73% reduction in tenant-visible 5xx waves for injected tests. Noted 0.15% increase in median streaming latency for unaffected flows; monitoring to continue.
2025-02-17: Support runbook drafted and tested by on-call; one customer opt-in executed successfully. Added request_fingerprint to trace spans for impacted sessions.
2025-02-20: Metrics stabilized. Moving to broader 25% rollout pending peer review and post-canary incident retro. Follow-up ticket created to harden runtime scheduler (ENG-762411).
notes: Do not conflate this with generic retry-throttle fixes; this is targeted at streaming idle-progress stalls. Ensure SDK compatibility tests run (sdk-js, sdk-python) before full rollout.
